newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Germany's Kinkel urges end to Albania poll deadlock.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Kinkel urges end to Albania poll deadlock.

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel has spoken with Albanian Prime Minister Bashkim Fino, calling on the country's politicians to end a deadlock over planned elections, state-run news agency ATA said on Monday.
ATA said that Kinkel and Fino spoke by telephone late Sunday. Kinkel urged politicians to find a compromise so the elections could go ahead on June 29 as planned.
"This is in the interests of the Albanians and of the international community, which is committed to help Albania overcome the crisis," ATA quoted Kinkel as saying.
Most political parties are threatening to boycott the election, regarded as vital to restore order in Albania after it was engulfed by anarchy and riots in February and March.

Fino has been leading talks to end the crisis, hoping to persuade President Sali Berisha and his former ruling Democratic Party to agree to changes in the election law, which forced most parties to threaten the boycott.
The parties say the law favours Berisha and the Democrats and have come up with a package of changes they want.
Kinkel's is the latest in a string of warnings from Western governments that they want Albania's politicians to come to a compromise otherwise aid and support may be withheld.
The European Union, Italy and the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) have all called on Albanian politicians to solve the crisis.
